{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ct-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"8b1cd13294cb0ab45e35ec71fd7865aac65a108daef9a5791fcfe689f340287b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ct-class-d:lineage:68","source_registry_sha256":"07bbe76598f0084cdb2ee450c7050097675dacd13ccc4c40045c307297557e80","source_liveness_sha256":"8fea57e2daef73f0a94408791d2027c4fc2c9799e8d48060efecbf84d96aedf5"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Alcohol, drugs and the law","heading":"C — Alcohol, drugs and the law","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Alcohol, drugs and the law

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A35
Alcohol rides in over forty percent of fatal crashes, any sip lifts crash odds, and green drivers suffer worse than veterans. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A35
Drinking drivers risk stiff fines, pricier insurance, lost licenses and jail cells. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A35
Drink travels stomach to blood to brain, first numbing judgment itself, so overdose announces only past the point of return like late felt sunburn. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A35
Rising doses dull reflexes, sight, alertness, distance and speed math, other car tracking, and basic vehicle control. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A35
Safest counsel is never drive after drinking, since any dose can impair and arrest, and under twenty one a single drink may suffice. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A35
One drink means a shot and a half of eighty proof liquor, a regular twelve ounce beer, or a five ounce wine, while exotic mixes can pack several. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A35
Coffee, air, exercise and cold showers never hurry sobriety; only passing time does. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A35
Party smart by rotating a dry designated driver among two plus friends, or by riding transit and cabs home. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A35
Headache, cold, allergy and nerve pills, prescription or store bought, can sedate and warp reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness like liquor or worse. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A35
Read every drug label for driving warnings, quiz doctors or druggists when unsure, and never mix pills with alcohol lest effects multiply toward sickness or death. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A35
Drunk driving draws court plus Commissioner penalties: a blood, breath or urine test, then on failure at least forty five suspended days plus an ignition interlock for six months minimum, longer with priors. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A35
Under twenty one zero tolerance treats any measurable drink, two hundredths percent and up on roads or private land, as arrestable, with failure costing forty five days and a year minimum interlock. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A35
Refusing every test at any age still costs forty five days plus a year minimum interlock, stretching with priors. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A36
Teen convictions for restriction breaks, speeding, reckless driving, street racing or phone use all suspend sixteen and seventeen year old licenses or licensing privileges. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A36
First restriction breaks cost thirty days plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines, while later ones cost six months or until eighteen, whichever lasts longer, plus the same money. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A36
Teen phone and texting tickets ladder thirty days, then ninety, then six months, each plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A36
Teen speeding twenty plus over ladders sixty days, then ninety, then six months, each plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A36
Teen GDL and reckless counts open six months plus fees and fines or up to thirty jail days, then year long suspensions with fines or up to a year locked, second and third times alike. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A36
Teen street racing opens six months plus fees and fines or up to a year locked, then year long suspensions with the same money or jail, second and third times alike. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A37
Someone under eighteen cannot be considered a youthful offender for negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, evading responsibility after a crash resulting in death or serious injury, or driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs [A37].
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A37
Youthful findings for reckless, suspended or property flight driving, street racing and officer eluding still reach DMV for license suspensions. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A37
Blue flashing or wailing stops want a right edge park clear of crossings, frozen cabin movement, wheel and visible hands, papers on request only, shut doors, seated waiting and lit domes by night. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A37
Contested tickets get fought in court, never argued roadside with the officer. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A37
Retraining school teaching operation basics, attitude versus aggression, and safe habits awaits drivers twenty four and under after two moving or suspension counts and older drivers after three. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A37
Teen retraining triggers include permit breaches, GDL breaches, and any under eighteen phone touching even hands free. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A37
One more moving count within three retrained years suspends the license at least thirty days. [A37]
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
